context:
Extract-with-generics. The two benchmark classes are not identical; they
parameterize over different ResultT / OperationT. The extraction must
preserve that parameterization, not collapse it.

Sequence each migration: introduce base, migrate ONE family, run tests,
commit; then migrate the second family. Do not bundle. The reason the
parent dedup TODO refused to touch this was bundle risk.
description:
Quality plan supplement - duplication workstream follow-up. Tracks
residual R-08 from
`quality-consolidate-duplicate-code-clusters` (see
docs/development/duplication-residuals.md).

`transaction_primitives` and `write_primitives` ship near-identical
`Benchmark` and `Operations` base classes - operation registry,
dispatch, reporting scaffolding - but with type signatures parameterized
over benchmark-specific result/operation types. Inventory measured the
duplication at three clusters: 101, 93, and 71 lines (~265 lines total)
across two 1300+ line files.

The dedup TODO deliberately deferred this because:
  - Multi-day refactor (extraction needs generics over the
    result/operation type parameter, plus a shared registry contract)
  - Touches benchmark execution path used by ACID tests - non-trivial
    test surface
  - Per-cluster scope of the parent dedup TODO was capped at ≤4 hours

This TODO does the extraction in reviewable slices and is the explicit
destination flagged by R-08.

anti_patterns.dont: collapse ResultT / OperationT into a single concrete type
anti_patterns.why: that loses type safety the existing classes provide

anti_patterns.dont: extract methods that genuinely differ between the two families
anti_patterns.instead: the survey in w1 must classify each method as shared vs divergent
anti_patterns.why: the diff exists for a reason

anti_patterns.dont: migrate both families in one commit
anti_patterns.why: review needs to see each migration in isolation

preserves.behavior: ACID test results unchanged at every scale factor
All transaction_primitives + write_primitives tests pass on every backend (DuckDB / Postgres / SQLite at minimum)
Result-model field names and types unchanged on the public surface (only the implementation moves)
Runtime behavior of every transaction_primitives + write_primitives benchmark unchanged

verifications.command: uv run --with pylint --with pandas --with polars pylint --disable=all --enable=duplicate-code --min-similarity-lines=15 benchbox/core/transaction_primitives/benchmark.py benchbox/core/transaction_primitives/operations.py benchbox/core/write_primitives/benchmark.py benchbox/core/write_primitives/operations.py 2>&1 | grep -c 'R0801'
verifications.description: Pylint R0801 count drops to 0 in the four target files (catalog/schema/dataframe_ops files are out-of-scope and retain pre-existing clusters)

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/unit/core/transaction_primitives/ tests/unit/core/write_primitives/ -q
uv run benchbox run --platform duckdb --benchmark transaction_primitives --scale 0.01 --dry-run /tmp/preview
verifications.description: ACID test runs cleanly on DuckDB

work_units.summary: Survey both Benchmark + Operations classes side-by-side: produce diff table of (shared method, divergent method, divergent type signature). Identify the minimal generic surface.
Introduce TransactionalBenchmarkBase[ResultT, OperationT] under benchbox/core/transactional/. Migrate transaction_primitives.Benchmark to inherit; one commit.
Migrate write_primitives.Benchmark onto TransactionalBenchmarkBase[ResultT, OperationT]; verify type params bind cleanly. One commit.
Introduce OperationsRegistryBase[OperationT]; migrate transaction_primitives.Operations and write_primitives.Operations one at a time.
Re-run pylint duplicate-code at 15-line threshold over both modules; confirm the three R-08 clusters drop out. Update docs/development/duplication-residuals.md.
